title: Звонок Елены и паника поваров  (Elena's Call and the Cooks' Panic)

segments.t: Elena Pavlovna calls Viktor Petrovich to thank him for the wonderful surprise dish and agrees to meet him in an hour. Meanwhile, the cooks realize that Chef Barinov tasted the fugu fish himself and begins feeling numb, sparking full-blown panic in the kitchen.
Тогда что же, встретимся через час?
А что, там холодно, быстрее отойдет?
Now let's go back through the conversation line by line.
'Elena Pavlovna, forgive me, my...' Notice how Russian expresses 'Elena' and 'my' with crisp inflection rather than helper words. Vika answers right away.
'Believe me, it was absolutely delightful.' Vika anchors the line on 'believe!', while 'delightful' completes the thought.
'I am glad that you liked it.' Notice how Russian expresses 'I' and 'liked' with crisp inflection rather than helper words.
'I thank you.' Notice how Russian expresses 'I' and 'to thank' with crisp inflection rather than helper words. Vika answers right away.
'It is nothing, nothing at all, do not worry.' In Russian, the idea of 'nothing' flows naturally into 'worry' without extra filler words.
'Excuse me. It is nothing.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'excuse me' and finishing on 'nothing'.
'Everything is fine.' Chef Viktor brings out the contrast between 'all' and 'order' in a few short words. Vika answers right away.
'Hello, Viktor Petrovich.' The meaning hinges on 'hello' working together with 'Petrovich' in spoken Russian.
Тогда что же, встретимся через час?
'Then what do you say we meet in an hour?' Elena brings out the contrast between 'then' and 'what' in a few short words.
'I will be driving my car.' Chef Viktor anchors the line on 'I', while 'car' completes the thought. Vika answers right away.
'We have to stop him.' In Russian, the idea of 'at' flows naturally into 'to stop' without extra filler words.
'It makes no difference now.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'this' before landing on 'equal'.
А что, там холодно, быстрее отойдет?

'What, since it is cold in there, will it wear off faster?' Notice how Russian expresses 'and' and 'will leave' with crisp inflection rather than helper words. Alright, let's hear the whole conversation once more from start to finish.
Тогда что же, встретимся через час?
А что, там холодно, быстрее отойдет?
